berkowitz1977.thermal_correction_assumption: All vibrational and three rotational degrees of freedom contribute to dissociative ionization; the paper adds the mean internal energy to the observed onset.
berkowitz1977.uncertainty_note: Abstract p2183 and body p2185 give different error bars. Both are preserved without selecting a statistical confidence convention or assuming a typographical cause.
berkowitz1977.formation_enthalpy_auxiliary_source: JANAF 1968, reference 13; no new harmonized molecular/atomic formation energy is inferred from this quotation.
berkowitz1977.parent_threshold_note: SSO parent-ion threshold is not the SO ionization energy subtracted in the fragment cycle.
berkowitz1977.contamination_checks: SO2 and SOCl2 fragment thresholds/yields and lack of free SO signal are examined in section III.B; original intensities are not re-reduced here.

norwood1989.limitations: Tables 1-2 describe SO+ and SSO+ vibrational/electronic states; they do not establish a neutral SSO high-temperature partition function. Quoted uncertainties have no stated statistical confidence level.

interpretation: The 1977 0 K threshold minus the 1989 SO adiabatic ionization energy gives 3.451 eV for SSO -> S + SO, the cycle used by Lodders 2004. Do not subtract SSO parent ionization or add the 0.051 eV thermal correction twice.
The fragment energy is not total atomization to 2 S + O. Full modern atomization requires consistent auxiliary SO/atomic energies and their correlations.
Lodders, Gurvich and ATcT share the 1977 experimental ancestry; the two newly inspected papers do not independently validate three thermochemical evaluations.
Primary experimental access gaps are closed. The Gurvich thermal inventory, original fit inputs and remaining modern theoretical/numerical provenance are still incomplete.
